newsitem.title: USA: Start of Lyondell-Citgo refinery upgrade imminent.
newsitem.headline: Start of Lyondell-Citgo refinery upgrade imminent.

text.p: Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co is "debugging" a $1.1 billion upgrade of its Houston refinery and start-up is "imminent," a Citgo Petroleum Corp official said on Tuesday.
The company had hoped to bring a new crude distillation unit and delayed coker on line last Sunday, but ran into problems with the compressor, said the official, who requested anonymity.
Traders noted that some of the heavy sour crude that the refinery was expected to process hit the market late last week, prompting speculation of snags at the Houston facility.
Technicians repaired the compressor's gear box vibration, but found "another glitch" last night when they attempted a start-up, the official said.
"We're mechanicially complete...and we're in the start-up phase," he added.
The upgrade is part of a Venezuelan crude oil supply agreement that will give Citgo, the domestic unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA, a 40 percent stake in the refinery.
The rated capacity of the refinery will remain at 265,000 barrels per day (bpd), but the upgrade will allow the facility to process 200,000 bpd of 17-API gravity Venezuelan crude.
